federal_note: Federal programs (DTC, Child Disability Benefit, RDSP, Canada Child Benefit, Canada Disability Benefit for adults, Jordan's Principle, Inuit Child First) apply everywhere; see data/programs.json.

programs.name: Family Support for Children with Disabilities (FSCD)
programs.what: Alberta pays for help your family needs because of your child's disability. This can include respite (a break for you), aides, child care help, counselling, and autism therapy. Your income does not matter.
programs.amount: Individual agreement based on assessed needs; no fixed maximum published.
who: Your child has a long-term disability, or is waiting to be diagnosed.
You live in Alberta and are your child's guardian.
steps: Apply online at Alberta Supports, or call 1-877-644-9992.
Send proof your child is a citizen or permanent resident, and a letter from a doctor or therapist.
A worker will call you to talk about what you need.
programs.nickname: FSCD (Alberta help for kids with disabilities)

programs.name: Alberta Disability Assistance Program (ADAP) and AISH
programs.what: Monthly money for adults with a disability who can't cover their basic costs. ADAP is the newer program. AISH is the older one.
programs.amount: As of July 2, 2026: ADAP core benefit $1,740/month (single); AISH maximum $1,940/month (Alberta financial benefits summary, checked 2026-10-17).
who: You must have low income and few savings.
steps: Try the online benefit estimator first.

programs.name: Alberta Child and Family Benefit (ACFB)
programs.what: Extra tax-free money for families with kids under 18 and lower or middle income. It comes with the Canada Child Benefit.
programs.amount: No fixed amount published; check the official page.
who: You have kids under 18 and file taxes.
steps: File your taxes every year. The money comes on its own.

programs.name: Alberta Aids to Daily Living (AADL)
programs.what: Helps pay for medical equipment and supplies. This can include some talking devices.
programs.amount: No fixed amount published; check the official page.
who: Your child has a long-term disability or illness.
A trained therapist (called an authorizer) checks what your child needs.
steps: Ask your child's therapist to do an AADL check.

programs.name: Jordan's Principle (First Nations children)
programs.what: Money from the federal government for First Nations kids. It can pay for therapy, respite (a break for you while someone else cares for your child), talking devices, and equipment. It works in every province, on or off reserve.
programs.amount: Case by case; no fixed amount.
who: Your child is First Nations and under 19
steps: Call 1-855-572-4453. The line is open 24 hours a day.
Or apply online on the Indigenous Services Canada website.
programs.nickname: Jordan's Principle (help for First Nations kids)
